1→
  BIP: 39
  Layer: Applications
  Title: Mnemonic code for generating deterministic keys
  Authors: Marek Palatinus 
           Pavol Rusnak 
           Aaron Voisine 
           Sean Bowe 
  Comments-Summary: Unanimously Discourage for implementation
10→  Comments-URI: https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/wiki/Comments:BIP-0039
  Status: Deployed
  Type: Specification
  Assigned: 2013-09-10
  License: MIT
==Abstract== This BIP describes the implementation of a mnemonic code or mnemonic sentence -- 20→a group of easy to remember words -- for the generation of deterministic wallets. It consists of two parts: generating the mnemonic and converting it into a binary seed. This seed can be later used to generate deterministic wallets using BIP-0032 or similar methods. ==Copyright== This BIP falls under the MIT License. 30→==Motivation== A mnemonic code or sentence is superior for human interaction compared to the handling of raw binary or hexadecimal representations of a wallet seed. The sentence could be written on paper or spoken over the telephone. This guide is meant to be a way to transport computer-generated randomness with a human-readable transcription. It's not a way to process user-created sentences (also known as brainwallets) into a wallet seed. 40→==Generating the mnemonic== The mnemonic must encode entropy in a multiple of 32 bits. With more entropy security is improved but the sentence length increases. We refer to the initial entropy length as ENT. The allowed size of ENT is 128-256 bits. First, an initial entropy of ENT bits is generated. A checksum is generated by taking the first ENT / 32 bits of its SHA256 hash. This checksum is appended to the end of the initial entropy. Next, these concatenated bits are split into groups of 11 bits, each encoding a number from 0-2047, serving 50→as an index into a wordlist. Finally, we convert these numbers into words and use the joined words as a mnemonic sentence. The following table describes the relation between the initial entropy length (ENT), the checksum length (CS), and the length of the generated mnemonic sentence (MS) in words. 
CS = ENT / 32
MS = (ENT + CS) / 11
60→
|  ENT  | CS | ENT+CS |  MS  |
+-------+----+--------+------+
|  128  |  4 |   132  |  12  |
|  160  |  5 |   165  |  15  |
|  192  |  6 |   198  |  18  |
|  224  |  7 |   231  |  21  |
|  256  |  8 |   264  |  24  |
70→==Wordlist== An ideal wordlist has the following characteristics: a) smart selection of words - the wordlist is created in such a way that it's enough to type the first four letters to unambiguously identify the word b) similar words avoided - word pairs like "build" and "built", "woman" and "women", or "quick" and "quickly" 80→ not only make remembering the sentence difficult but are also more error

91→==From mnemonic to seed==

A user may decide to protect their mnemonic with a passphrase. If a passphrase is not
present, an empty string "" is used instead.

To create a binary seed from the mnemonic, we use the PBKDF2 function with a mnemonic
sentence (in UTF-8 NFKD) used as the password and the string "mnemonic" + passphrase (again
in UTF-8 NFKD) used as the salt. The iteration count is set to 2048 and HMAC-SHA512 is used as

  BIP: 44
  Layer: Applications
  Title: Multi-Account Hierarchy for Deterministic Wallets
  Authors: Marek Palatinus 
           Pavol Rusnak 
  Comments-Summary: Mixed review (one person)
  Comments-URI: https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/wiki/Comments:BIP-0044
  Status: Deployed
10→  Type: Specification
  Assigned: 2014-04-24
  Requires: 32, 43
==Abstract== This BIP defines a logical hierarchy for deterministic wallets based on an algorithm described in BIP-0032 (BIP32 from now on) and purpose scheme described in BIP-0043 (BIP43 from now on). 20→ This BIP is a particular application of BIP43. ==Motivation== The hierarchy proposed in this paper is quite comprehensive. It allows the handling of multiple coins, multiple accounts, external and internal chains per account and millions of addresses per chain. ==Path levels== 30→ We define the following 5 levels in BIP32 path: 
m / purpose' / coin_type' / account' / change / address_index
Apostrophe in the path indicates that BIP32 hardened derivation is used. Each level has a special meaning, described in the chapters below. 40→ ===Purpose=== Purpose is a constant set to 44' (or 0x8000002C) following the BIP43 recommendation. It indicates that the subtree of this node is used according to this specification. Hardened derivation is used at this level. ===Coin type=== 50→One master node (seed) can be used for unlimited number of independent cryptocoins such as Bitcoin, Litecoin or Namecoin. However, sharing the same space for various cryptocoins has some disadvantages. This level creates a separate subtree for every cryptocoin, avoiding reusing addresses across cryptocoins and improving privacy issues. Coin type is a constant, set for each cryptocoin. Cryptocoin developers may ask for registering unused number for their project. 60→The list of already allocated coin types is in the chapter "Registered coin types" below. Hardened derivation is used at this level. ===Account=== This level splits the key space into independent user identities, so the wallet never mixes the coins across different accounts. 70→Users can use these accounts to organize the funds in the same fashion as bank accounts; for donation purposes (where all addresses are considered public), for saving purposes, for common expenses etc. Accounts are numbered from index 0 in sequentially increasing manner. This number is used as child index in BIP32 derivation. Hardened derivation is used at this level. 80→Software should prevent a creation of an account if a previous account does not

72→====Private parent key → private child key====

The function CKDpriv((k<sub>par</sub>, c<sub>par</sub>), i) → (k<sub>i</sub>, c<sub>i</sub>) computes a child extended private key from the parent extended private key:
* Check whether i ≥ 2<sup>31</sup> (whether the child is a hardened key).
** If so (hardened child): let I = HMAC-SHA512(Key = c<sub>par</sub>, Data = 0x00 || ser<sub>256</sub>(k<sub>par</sub>) || ser<sub>32</sub>(i)). (Note: The 0x00 pads the private key to make it 33 bytes long.)
** If not (normal child): let I = HMAC-SHA512(Key = c<sub>par</sub>, Data = ser<sub>P</sub>(point(k<sub>par</sub>)) || ser<sub>32</sub>(i)).
* Split I into two 32-byte sequences, I<sub>L</sub> and I<sub>R</sub>.
* The returned child key k<sub>i</sub> is parse<sub>256</sub>(I<sub>L</sub>) + k<sub>par</sub> (mod n).
80→* The returned chain code c<sub>i</sub> is I<sub>R</sub>.
* In case parse<sub>256</sub>(I<sub>L</sub>) ≥ n or k<sub>i</sub> = 0, the resulting key is invalid, and one should proceed with the next value for i. (Note: this has probability lower than 1 in 2<sup>127</sup>.)

The HMAC-SHA512 function is specified in [http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4231 RFC 4231].

====Public parent key → public child key====

The function CKDpub((K<sub>par</sub>, c<sub>par</sub>), i) → (K<sub>i</sub>, c<sub>i</sub>) computes a child extended public key from the parent extended public key. It is only defined for non-hardened child keys.
* Check whether i ≥ 2<sup>31</sup> (whether the child is a hardened key).
** If so (hardened child): return failure
90→** If not (normal child): let I = HMAC-SHA512(Key = c<sub>par</sub>, Data = ser<sub>P</sub>(K<sub>par</sub>) || ser<sub>32</sub>(i)).
* Split I into two 32-byte sequences, I<sub>L</sub> and I<sub>R</sub>.
* The returned child key K<sub>i</sub> is point(parse<sub>256</sub>(I<sub>L</sub>)) + K<sub>par</sub>.
* The returned chain code c<sub>i</sub> is I<sub>R</sub>.
* In case parse<sub>256</sub>(I<sub>L</sub>) ≥ n or K<sub>i</sub> is the point at infinity, the resulting key is invalid, and one should proceed with the next value for i.

====Private parent key → public child key====

The function N((k, c)) → (K, c) computes the extended public key corresponding to an extended private key (the "neutered" version, as it removes the ability to sign transactions).
* The returned key K is point(k).
100→* The returned chain code c is just the passed chain code.

To compute the public child key of a parent private key:
* N(CKDpriv((k<sub>par</sub>, c<sub>par</sub>), i)) (works always).
* CKDpub(N(k<sub>par</sub>, c<sub>par</sub>), i) (works only for non-hardened child keys).
The fact that they are equivalent is what makes non-hardened keys useful (one can derive child public keys of a given parent key without knowing any private key), and also what distinguishes them from hardened keys. The reason for not always using non-hardened keys (which are more useful) is security; see further below for more information.

====Public parent key → private child key====

This is not possible.
110→
===The key tree===

The next step is cascading several CKD constructions to build a tree. We start with one root, the master extended key m. By evaluating CKDpriv(m,i) for several values of i, we get a number of level-1 derived nodes. As each of these is again an extended key, CKDpriv can be applied to those as well.

To shorten notation, we will write CKDpriv(CKDpriv(CKDpriv(m,3<sub>H</sub>),2),5) as m/3<sub>H</sub>/2/5. Equivalently for public keys, we write CKDpub(CKDpub(CKDpub(M,3),2),5) as M/3/2/5. This results in the following identities:
* N(m/a/b/c) = N(m/a/b)/c = N(m/a)/b/c = N(m)/a/b/c = M/a/b/c.
* N(m/a<sub>H</sub>/b/c) = N(m/a<sub>H</sub>/b)/c = N(m/a<sub>H</sub>)/b/c.
However, N(m/a<sub>H</sub>) cannot be rewritten as N(m)/a<sub>H</sub>, as the latter is not possible.

120→Each leaf node in the tree corresponds to an actual key, while the internal nodes correspond to the collections of keys that descend from them. The chain codes of the leaf nodes are ignored, and only their embedded private or public key is relevant. Because of this construction, knowing an extended private key allows reconstruction of all descendant private keys and public keys, and knowing an extended public key allows reconstruction of all descendant non-hardened public keys.

* CKDpub(N(k<sub>par</sub>, c<sub>par</sub>), i) (works only for non-hardened child keys).
The fact that they are equivalent is what makes non-hardened keys useful (one can derive child public keys of a given parent key without knowing any private key), and also what distinguishes them from hardened keys. The reason for not always using non-hardened keys (which are more useful) is security; see further below for more information.

====Public parent key → private child key====

This is not possible.
110→
===The key tree===

The next step is cascading several CKD constructions to build a tree. We start with one root, the master extended key m. By evaluating CKDpriv(m,i) for several values of i, we get a number of level-1 derived nodes. As each of these is again an extended key, CKDpriv can be applied to those as well.

To shorten notation, we will write CKDpriv(CKDpriv(CKDpriv(m,3<sub>H</sub>),2),5) as m/3<sub>H</sub>/2/5. Equivalently for public keys, we write CKDpub(CKDpub(CKDpub(M,3),2),5) as M/3/2/5. This results in the following identities:
* N(m/a/b/c) = N(m/a/b)/c = N(m/a)/b/c = N(m)/a/b/c = M/a/b/c.
* N(m/a<sub>H</sub>/b/c) = N(m/a<sub>H</sub>/b)/c = N(m/a<sub>H</sub>)/b/c.
However, N(m/a<sub>H</sub>) cannot be rewritten as N(m)/a<sub>H</sub>, as the latter is not possible.

The chain codes of the leaf nodes are ignored, and only their embedded private or public key is relevant. Because of this construction, knowing an extended private key allows reconstruction of all descendant private keys and public keys, and knowing an extended public key allows reconstruction of all descendant non-hardened public keys.

* Split I into two 32-byte sequences, I<sub>L</sub> and I<sub>R</sub>.
* The returned child key k<sub>i</sub> is parse<sub>256</sub>(I<sub>L</sub>) + k<sub>par</sub> (mod n).
* The returned chain code c<sub>i</sub> is I<sub>R</sub>.
* In case parse<sub>256</sub>(I<sub>L</sub>) ≥ n or k<sub>i</sub> = 0, the resulting key is invalid, and one should proceed with the next value for i. (Note: this has probability lower than 1 in 2<sup>127</sup>.)

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
# Usage: start-sut.sh <name> <port> [extra env assignments...]
NAME="$1"
PORT="$2"
shift 2
WORKDIR="/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work"
INST="$WORKDIR/instances/$NAME"
mkdir -p "$INST"
KEY_FILE="$INST/key"
if [[ ! -f "$KEY_FILE" ]]; then
  openssl rand -hex 32 > "$KEY_FILE"
fi
export WALLET_ENCRYPTION_KEY="$(cat "$KEY_FILE")"
export RPC_URL="http://127.0.0.1:8545"
export USDC_TOKEN_ADDRESS="0x5aAeb6053F3E94C9b9A09f33669435E7Ef1BeAed"
export DATABASE_PATH="$INST/exchange.sqlite"
export HOST="127.0.0.1"
export PORT
export SESSION_TTL_SECONDS="${SESSION_TTL_SECONDS:-3600}"
# extra env from remaining args as KEY=VAL
for kv in "$@"; do
  export "$kv"
done
cd /tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-sut
# run via tsx so we don't need a dist build
nohup ./node_modules/.bin/tsx src/server.ts > "$WORKDIR/logs/${NAME}.stdout" 2> "$WORKDIR/logs/${NAME}.stderr" &
echo $! > "$INST/pid"
# wait for health
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  if curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "READY name=$NAME port=$PORT pid=$(cat "$INST/pid")"
    exit 0
  fi
  if ! kill -0 "$(cat "$INST/pid")" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "EXITED name=$NAME"
    echo "--- stderr ---"
    cat "$WORKDIR/logs/${NAME}.stderr" || true
    echo "--- stdout ---"
    cat "$WORKDIR/logs/${NAME}.stdout" || true
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 0.25
done
echo "TIMEOUT name=$NAME"
exit 1

register_login_addr() {
  local name="$1" port="$2" email="$3" outfile="$4"

  curl -sS -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:${port}/api/v1/auth/register" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --data "{\"email\":\"${email}\",\"password\":\"${pass}\"}" | tee "${outfile}.reg.json"
  echo
  local login
  login=$(curl -sS -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:${port}/api/v1/auth/login" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --data "{\"email\":\"${email}\",\"password\":\"${pass}\"}")
  echo "$login" | tee "${outfile}.login.json"
  echo
  local token
  token=$(python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["token"])' <<<"$login")
  curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:${port}/api/v1/deposit-address?asset=ETH" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${token}" | tee "${outfile}.addr.json"
  echo
}

query_db() {
  local db="$1" sql="$2"
  python3 - "$db" "$sql" <<'PY'
import sqlite3,sys,json
con=sqlite3.connect(sys.argv[1])
con.row_factory=sqlite3.Row
rows=con.execute(sys.argv[2]).fetchall()

PY
}

  --data '{"email":"bob@example.com","password":"Sup3rSecreta"}' | tee "$OUT/i03-B.reg.json"

  "SELECT account_id, address_index, address, derivation_path, network, chain_id FROM deposit_addresses ORDER BY address_index" \
  | tee "$OUT/i03-map.json"

  "SELECT id, type, payload, created_at FROM domain_events ORDER BY id" \

  --data '{"email":"Audit.User@Example.COM","password":"Sup3rSecreta"}' | tee "$OUT/main-login-ok.json"

set -euo pipefail
OUT=/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work/out

MN24=$(python3 -c 'print(" ".join(["abandon"]*23+["art"]))')

echo
cat "$OUT/i03-internal-auth.body"; echo

echo "===== destroy I1 and start I2 ====="
kill -9 "$(cat $WORKDIR/instances/i1/pid)" || true
rm -rf "$WORKDIR/instances/i1"
/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work/start-sut.sh i2 3416

  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"email":"a2@example.com","password":"Sup3rSecreta"}' > "$OUT/i2.reg.json"

wait $ANVIL_PID 2>/dev/null || true

payload.data: He revisado el briefing y la rúbrica.
Voy a evaluar los ATs indicados usando el procedimiento completo de la rúbrica, y luego emitiré los resultados en `resultados.
Primero, voy a procesar los ATs que mencionas: AT-06- 03-07, AT-06-01-11, AT-06-01-13 y AT-06-03-08.

rawInput.command:
set -euo pipefail
WORKDIR=/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work
OUT=$WORKDIR/out
SUT=/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-sut
TSX=$SUT/node_modules/.bin/tsx

echo "===== stop i11 ====="
kill -9 "$(cat $WORKDIR/instances/i11/pid)" || true
sleep 0.5
python3 - <<'PY'
import sqlite3,json
con=sqlite3.connect("/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work/instances/i11/exchange.sqlite")
row=con.execute("select length(encrypted_seed) as n, hex(encrypted_seed) as blob from wallet_secret").fetchone()
open("/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work/out/i11-blob-before.txt","w").write(f"n={row[0]}\nblob={row[1]}\n")
print(f"n={row[0]}")
print(f"blob={row[1]}")
print("seed_count", con.execute("select count(*) from wallet_secret").fetchone()[0])
PY

echo "===== AT-06-01-11 restart WITHOUT key ====="
cd $SUT
set +e
env -u WALLET_ENCRYPTION_KEY \
  RPC_URL="http://127.0.0.1:8545" \
  USDC_TOKEN_ADDRESS="0x5aAeb6053F3E94C9b9A09f33669435E7Ef1BeAed" \
  DATABASE_PATH="$WORKDIR/instances/i11/exchange.sqlite" \
  HOST="127.0.0.1" PORT="3421" \
  $TSX src/server.ts > "$OUT/at-06-01-11-nokey.stdout" 2> "$OUT/at-06-01-11-nokey.stderr"
echo $? > "$OUT/at-06-01-11-nokey.exit"
set -e
echo "exit=$(cat $OUT/at-06-01-11-nokey.exit)"
echo "stderr:"; cat "$OUT/at-06-01-11-nokey.stderr"

echo "===== AT-06-01-11 restart with WRONG key ====="
WRONG=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
set +e
WALLET_ENCRYPTION_KEY="$WRONG" \
  RPC_URL="http://127.0.0.1:8545" \
  USDC_TOKEN_ADDRESS="0x5aAeb6053F3E94C9b9A09f33669435E7Ef1BeAed" \
  DATABASE_PATH="$WORKDIR/instances/i11/exchange.sqlite" \
  HOST="127.0.0.1" PORT="3422" \
  $TSX src/server.ts > "$OUT/at-06-01-11-badkey.stdout" 2> "$OUT/at-06-01-11-badkey.stderr"
echo $? > "$OUT/at-06-01-11-badkey.exit"
set -e
echo "exit=$(cat $OUT/at-06-01-11-badkey.exit)"
echo "stderr:"; cat "$OUT/at-06-01-11-badkey.stderr"

echo "===== blob after failed restarts ====="
python3 - <<'PY'
import sqlite3
con=sqlite3.connect("/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work/instances/i11/exchange.sqlite")
row=con.execute("select length(encrypted_seed) as n, hex(encrypted_seed) as blob from wallet_secret").fetchone()
before=open("/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work/out/i11-blob-before.txt").read().strip().splitlines()
before_blob=before[1].split("=",1)[1]
print(f"n={row[0]}")
print(f"blob={row[1]}")
print("seed_count", con.execute("select count(*) from wallet_secret").fetchone()[0])
print("blob_intact", row[1]==before_blob)
open("/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work/out/i11-blob-after.txt","w").write(f"n={row[0]}\nblob={row[1]}\nintact={row[1]==before_blob}\n")
PY

echo "===== AT-06-01-13: stop i03, corrupt lowest address, restart ====="
kill -9 "$(cat $WORKDIR/instances/i03/pid)" || true
sleep 0.5
python3 - <<'PY'
import sqlite3
con=sqlite3.connect("/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work/instances/i03/exchange.sqlite")
con.execute("PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(FULL)")
row=con.execute("select account_id, address_index, address from deposit_addresses order by address_index limit 1").fetchone()
print("before", row)
addr=row[2]
# flip last hex nibble while keeping 42-char 0x form
last='3' if addr[-1].lower()!='3' else '4'
new=addr[:-1]+last
print("new", new)
con.execute("update deposit_addresses set address=? where address_index=?", (new, row[1]))
con.commit()
row2=con.execute("select account_id, address_index, address from deposit_addresses order by address_index limit 1").fetchone()
print("after", row2)
seed_hex=con.execute("select hex(encrypted_seed) from wallet_secret").fetchone()[0]
open("/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work/out/i03-seed-before-integrity.txt","w").write(seed_hex+"\n")
print("seed_len", len(seed_hex)//2)
PY

KEY=$(cat $WORKDIR/instances/i03/key)
set +e
WALLET_ENCRYPTION_KEY="$KEY" \
  RPC_URL="http://127.0.0.1:8545" \
  USDC_TOKEN_ADDRESS="0x5aAeb6053F3E94C9b9A09f33669435E7Ef1BeAed" \
  DATABASE_PATH="$WORKDIR/instances/i03/exchange.sqlite" \
  HOST="127.0.0.1" PORT="3423" \
  $TSX src/server.ts > "$OUT/at-06-01-13.stdout" 2> "$OUT/at-06-01-13.stderr"
echo $? > "$OUT/at-06-01-13.exit"
set -e
echo "exit=$(cat $OUT/at-06-01-13.exit)"
echo "stderr:"; cat "$OUT/at-06-01-13.stderr"
echo "stdout:"; cat "$OUT/at-06-01-13.stdout"
# confirm not listening
curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:3423/health" && echo HEALTH_UNEXPECTED || echo "health_unreachable_ok"

python3 - <<'PY'
import sqlite3
con=sqlite3.connect("/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work/instances/i03/exchange.sqlite")
print("seed_count", con.execute("select count(*) from wallet_secret").fetchone()[0])
print("addr_count", con.execute("select count(*) from deposit_addresses").fetchone()[0])
print("lowest", con.execute("select address_index, address from deposit_addresses order by address_index limit 1").fetchone())
seed_hex=con.execute("select hex(encrypted_seed) from wallet_secret").fetchone()[0]
before=open("/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work/out/i03-seed-before-integrity.txt").read().strip()
print("seed_unchanged", seed_hex==before)
PY

rawOutput.command:
set -euo pipefail
WORKDIR=/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work
OUT=$WORKDIR/out
SUT=/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-sut
TSX=$SUT/node_modules/.bin/tsx

echo "===== stop i11 ====="
kill -9 "$(cat $WORKDIR/instances/i11/pid)" || true
sleep 0.5
python3 - <<'PY'
import sqlite3,json
con=sqlite3.connect("/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work/instances/i11/exchange.sqlite")
row=con.execute("select length(encrypted_seed) as n, hex(encrypted_seed) as blob from wallet_secret").fetchone()
open("/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work/out/i11-blob-before.txt","w").write(f"n={row[0]}\nblob={row[1]}\n")
print(f"n={row[0]}")
print(f"blob={row[1]}")
print("seed_count", con.execute("select count(*) from wallet_secret").fetchone()[0])
PY

echo "===== AT-06-01-11 restart WITHOUT key ====="
cd $SUT
set +e
env -u WALLET_ENCRYPTION_KEY \
  RPC_URL="http://127.0.0.1:8545" \
  USDC_TOKEN_ADDRESS="0x5aAeb6053F3E94C9b9A09f33669435E7Ef1BeAed" \
  DATABASE_PATH="$WORKDIR/instances/i11/exchange.sqlite" \
  HOST="127.0.0.1" PORT="3421" \
  $TSX src/server.ts > "$OUT/at-06-01-11-nokey.stdout" 2> "$OUT/at-06-01-11-nokey.stderr"
echo $? > "$OUT/at-06-01-11-nokey.exit"
set -e
echo "exit=$(cat $OUT/at-06-01-11-nokey.exit)"
echo "stderr:"; cat "$OUT/at-06-01-11-nokey.stderr"

echo "===== AT-06-01-11 restart with WRONG key ====="
WRONG=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
set +e
WALLET_ENCRYPTION_KEY="$WRONG" \
  RPC_URL="http://127.0.0.1:8545" \
  USDC_TOKEN_ADDRESS="0x5aAeb6053F3E94C9b9A09f33669435E7Ef1BeAed" \
  DATABASE_PATH="$WORKDIR/instances/i11/exchange.sqlite" \
  HOST="127.0.0.1" PORT="3422" \
  $TSX src/server.ts > "$OUT/at-06-01-11-badkey.stdout" 2> "$OUT/at-06-01-11-badkey.stderr"
echo $? > "$OUT/at-06-01-11-badkey.exit"
set -e
echo "exit=$(cat $OUT/at-06-01-11-badkey.exit)"
echo "stderr:"; cat "$OUT/at-06-01-11-badkey.stderr"

echo "===== blob after failed restarts ====="
python3 - <<'PY'
import sqlite3
con=sqlite3.connect("/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work/instances/i11/exchange.sqlite")
row=con.execute("select length(encrypted_seed) as n, hex(encrypted_seed) as blob from wallet_secret").fetchone()
before=open("/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work/out/i11-blob-before.txt").read().strip().splitlines()
before_blob=before[1].split("=",1)[1]
print(f"n={row[0]}")
print(f"blob={row[1]}")
print("seed_count", con.execute("select count(*) from wallet_secret").fetchone()[0])
print("blob_intact", row[1]==before_blob)
open("/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work/out/i11-blob-after.txt","w").write(f"n={row[0]}\nblob={row[1]}\nintact={row[1]==before_blob}\n")
PY

echo "===== AT-06-01-13: stop i03, corrupt lowest address, restart ====="
kill -9 "$(cat $WORKDIR/instances/i03/pid)" || true
sleep 0.5
python3 - <<'PY'
import sqlite3
con=sqlite3.connect("/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work/instances/i03/exchange.sqlite")
con.execute("PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(FULL)")
row=con.execute("select account_id, address_index, address from deposit_addresses order by address_index limit 1").fetchone()
print("before", row)
addr=row[2]
# flip last hex nibble while keeping 42-char 0x form
last='3' if addr[-1].lower()!='3' else '4'
new=addr[:-1]+last
print("new", new)
con.execute("update deposit_addresses set address=? where address_index=?", (new, row[1]))
con.commit()
row2=con.execute("select account_id, address_index, address from deposit_addresses order by address_index limit 1").fetchone()
print("after", row2)
seed_hex=con.execute("select hex(encrypted_seed) from wallet_secret").fetchone()[0]
open("/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work/out/i03-seed-before-integrity.txt","w").write(seed_hex+"\n")
print("seed_len", len(seed_hex)//2)
PY

KEY=$(cat $WORKDIR/instances/i03/key)
set +e
WALLET_ENCRYPTION_KEY="$KEY" \
  RPC_URL="http://127.0.0.1:8545" \
  USDC_TOKEN_ADDRESS="0x5aAeb6053F3E94C9b9A09f33669435E7Ef1BeAed" \
  DATABASE_PATH="$WORKDIR/instances/i03/exchange.sqlite" \
  HOST="127.0.0.1" PORT="3423" \
  $TSX src/server.ts > "$OUT/at-06-01-13.stdout" 2> "$OUT/at-06-01-13.stderr"
echo $? > "$OUT/at-06-01-13.exit"
set -e
echo "exit=$(cat $OUT/at-06-01-13.exit)"
echo "stderr:"; cat "$OUT/at-06-01-13.stderr"
echo "stdout:"; cat "$OUT/at-06-01-13.stdout"
# confirm not listening
curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:3423/health" && echo HEALTH_UNEXPECTED || echo "health_unreachable_ok"

python3 - <<'PY'
import sqlite3
con=sqlite3.connect("/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work/instances/i03/exchange.sqlite")
print("seed_count", con.execute("select count(*) from wallet_secret").fetchone()[0])
print("addr_count", con.execute("select count(*) from deposit_addresses").fetchone()[0])
print("lowest", con.execute("select address_index, address from deposit_addresses order by address_index limit 1").fetchone())
seed_hex=con.execute("select hex(encrypted_seed) from wallet_secret").fetchone()[0]
before=open("/tmp/eval-wb/eval-p2-work/out/i03-seed-before-integrity.txt").read().strip()
print("seed_unchanged", seed_hex==before)
PY
